Avodah Zarah 65a:10.english: The mishna teaches: With regard to a gentile who rents a Jew’s donkey to carry wine used for a libation on it, its rental fee is forbidden. The Gemara asks: Why do I need this additional clause? This is the same as the first clause, as the principle is the same; only the example is different. The Gemara answers: It was necessary to teach the latter clause in order to teach that if the gentile rented the donkey to sit upon it, even if the gentile placed his lagin of wine used for a libation on it, its rental fee is permitted, as he did not pay at all for placing the lagin.

Avodah Zarah 65a:11.english: The Gemara asks: Is this to say that it is not the legal right of the renter to place a lagin upon the donkey, and because of this, carrying the lagin is not part of the terms of transport?

Avodah Zarah 65a:12.english: And the Gemara raises a contradiction to this from a baraita: With regard to one who rents a donkey to ride on, the renter may place on it his garment, his water lagin, and his food for that journey. Beyond those items, the donkey driver, who would take the renter on the journey, may prevent him from placing anything on the animal by saying that he does not wish to further burden the donkey. The donkey driver may place on it barley and hay for the donkey and his food for that first day alone. Beyond those items, the renter may prevent him from placing anything on the animal, on the grounds that it will inhibit its progress.

Avodah Zarah 65a:13.english: Abaye said: Granted that it is the legal right of the renter to place a lagin upon the donkey, but in any event, if he does not place it on the donkey, can we say to the driver: Deduct the fee of his lagin from the rental? Since the donkey driver will not deduct any amount from the rental fee if he does not place the lagin on the donkey, therefore, even if he does place it, the rental fee is not forbidden.

Avodah Zarah 65a:14.english: With regard to the main point of the baraita, the Gemara asks: What are the circumstances? If locations in which one is able to purchase provisions on the way are common, the donkey driver can also prevent the renter from putting provisions on the donkey for the entire journey, and if locations in which one is able to purchase provisions along the way are uncommon, the renter cannot prevent the driver from taking his provisions for the journey either.

Avodah Zarah 65a:15.english: Rav Pappa said: No, it is necessary to teach this halakha with regard to a case where locations in which one is able to go to the trouble of purchasing provisions are common between station and station, i.e., one can find locations to purchase provisions along the way, but only with difficulty, and it will suffice for him for one day. A donkey driver is accustomed to troubling himself to purchase provisions along the way, and therefore it is not permitted for him to pack provisions for the entire journey on the donkey. A renter is not accustomed to troubling himself to purchase provisions along the way, and therefore he is allowed to pack all of his provisions.

Avodah Zarah 65a:16.hebrew: אבוה דרב אחא בריה דרב איקא הוה שפיך להו חמרא לעובדי כוכבים ואזיל מעבר להו מעברא ויהבו ליה גולפי באגרא אתו אמרו ליה לאביי א"ל כי קא טרח בהתירא קא טרח
Avodah Zarah 65a:16.english: The Gemara relates: The father of Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika, would pour wine which he sold to gentiles from the kankanim (jars) into their wineskins and go and ferry the gentiles over the crossing, and they would give him the gulfi (jugs) as payment. The gulfi that the wine had been stored in were included in the sale, and the gentiles would pay him by returning the gulfi. People came and told Abaye that Rav Ika's father was accepting a wage from the wine of gentiles. Abaye said to them: When he labored, he labored with permitted wine, since he was pouring kosher wine into the wineskins, and only subsequently the wine was rendered forbidden by being in the possession of the gentiles.

Avodah Zarah 65a:6.english: The mishna teaches: If the gentile hired the Jew to do other work with him, even if the gentile said to the Jew while he was working with him: Transport the barrel of libation wine for me from this place to that place, the Jew's wage is permitted. The Gemara notes that this formulation of the mishna indicates that this wage is permitted even if the gentile did not say to the Jew to transport the barrel of wine toward evening, meaning, toward the end of his workday.

Avodah Zarah 65a:7.english: And the Gemara raises a contradiction from a baraita: In the case of one who hires a laborer, and toward evening the employer said to the laborer: Transport this barrel of libation wine from this place to that place, his wage is permitted. By inference, the reason for this ruling is that the employer said it to the laborer toward evening, and therefore yes, it is permitted, as it is clear that the laborer has completed the labor for which he is being paid and the wage is not for moving the barrel. But if this happened during the entire day, not toward evening, this would not be permitted.

Avodah Zarah 65a:8.english: Abaye said: When we learned this in the mishna as well, we learned this with regard to the case where the employer said this toward evening. Rava said: This is not difficult. This case, where the wage is forbidden if it was not toward evening, is a case where the gentile employer said to the laborer: Transport one hundred barrels for me for one hundred perutot, in which case moving all of the barrels is considered a single task, and if one of the barrels was libation wine, the entire wage is forbidden. That case, in which the wage is permitted in any event, is a case where the employer said to the laborer: Transport each barrel for me for one peruta, such that each barrel is its own task.

Avodah Zarah 65a:9.english: And so it is taught in a baraita: In the case of one who hires a laborer and said to the laborer: Transport one hundred barrels for me for one hundred perutot, and a barrel of libation wine was found among them, his wage is forbidden. But if the employer said to the laborer: Transport each barrel for one peruta, and there was a barrel of libation wine among them, his wage is permitted.

Avodah Zarah 65b:2.english: The Gemara asks: But doesn’t he desire the preservation of the wine in the wineskins in that the wineskins should not be torn, as he would then need to return the gulfi he received in payment? The Gemara answers: It is a case where he stipulated with the gentile purchasers that even if the wineskins were to tear it would be at their expense and not his, and he would keep the gulfi in any event. Alternatively, it is a case where the gentile purchasers brought spare vessels [perisdakei] with them, so that they could pour the wine into them should the wineskins be torn, and therefore the preservation of the wineskins was not important to him.

Avodah Zarah 65b:3.english: The Gemara asks: But didn’t he ferry them over the crossing, which is laboring with forbidden wine? The Gemara answers: This is not a case where he was ferrying the wine over the crossing himself, as he made an arrangement with the ferrymen and said to the ferryman initially that the latter would ferry the buyers and the gulfi without payment. Alternatively, it was a case where he held special signal knots in collusion with the ferryman that he would ferry these people without payment. And in any case, Rav Ika's father himself was not laboring with them.

Avodah Zarah 65b:4.english: MISHNA: In the case of wine used for a libation that fell on grapes, one rinses them and they are permitted. But if the grapes were cracked, they are forbidden. In a case where the wine fell on figs or on dates, if there is sufficient wine in them to impart flavor, they are forbidden. And there was an incident involving Boethus ben Zunen, who transported dried figs in a ship, and a barrel of wine used for a libation broke and fell on them, and he asked the Sages as to the halakha, and the Sages deemed the figs permitted.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65a:10:1.hebrew: סיפא אצטריך ליה. לאשמועינן דאגרא לאו אלגין מקבל ליה, ושרי.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65a:10:2.hebrew: לגינו. של יין נסך לאו דרכיה לאותוביה, הלכך אגרא לאו עליה קא מתייהב.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65a:12:1.hebrew: של אותו הדרך. אפילו הוא מהלך ג' ימים.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65a:13:1.hebrew: מי אמרינן ליה. לחמר: נכי ליה פחת לו שכר הלגין? וכיון דכי לא מותיב לא מנכי, כי מותיב נמי אגרא לאו עליה מתחייב, ושרי.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65a:14:1.hebrew: ה"ד. דשוכר מניח עליה מזונות כל הדרך, וחמר אינו מניח אלא מזונות יום אחד.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65a:14:2.hebrew: אי דשכיח למזבן. בדרך הליכתן מוצאין מזונות ליקח כל שעה.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65a:15:1.hebrew: מאונא לאונא. ממסע למסע, מהלך יום אחד, כמו נטל ועבר תלתא אונין דסנחריב.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65a:6:1.hebrew: ואע"ג – דהעברת חבית לאו לעיתותי ערב, לאחר שנשלם כל זמן שכר פעולתו, אלא קודם גמר זמן שכירותו אמר לו: העבר חבית של יין נסך. קתני מתניתין: שכרו מותר? בתמיה!

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65a:7:1.hebrew: ולעיתותי ערב – דכבר נתחייב לו כל שכרו קודם העברת חבית.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65a:8:1.hebrew: רבא אמר – לעולם דלא אמר ליה לעיתותי ערב.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65a:8:2.hebrew: ולא קשיא – מתניתין דקתני מותר, כגון: העבר לי חבית בפרוטה, ונמצאת חבית של יין נסך ביניהן, שדי פרוטה לנהרא, או לא שקיל מיד עובד כוכבים, ואינך משתרו, דהא לא שייך שכר ההוא חבית בהדי אינך, דכל חדא קנין אגרא באפי נפשא. וברייתא דכי לא אמר ליה לעיתותי ערב הוי כל שכרו אסור, כגון דאמר ליה: העבר ק' חביות בק' פרוטות, דכל כמה דלא אעברינהו לכולהו לא יהיב ליה מידי, הלכך כולי אגרא שייך ביה.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65b:1:1.hebrew: הוה שפיך להו חמרא לעובדי כוכבים. הוא היה מוכר להם יין, ודרך למוכרי חביות של יין ליתן גם החביות ללוקחין. והכי אמרינן בהמפקיד (ב"מ מ:): איכא גולפי ושדריה, שהלוקח מוכרו בחנות משתכר בהן לבד מה שהוא משתכר ביין. ורב איקא הוה שפיך להו מגולפי שלקחו ממנו, ויהיב בזיקי דידהו.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65b:1:3.hebrew: ויהבו ליה גולפי. דזבון מיניה באגרא.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65b:1:5.hebrew: בדידיה קא טרח. שהיין אינו נאסר עד שמגיע לקרקעית של זיקי דידהו. זיקי של עור, גולפי של חרס. ולקמיה פריך: הא קא מעבר להו מעברא, דהיינו לאחר שנאסר.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65b:2:2.hebrew: דלא נצטרו זיקי. שלא יתבקעו הנודות שלהם, ויצטרכו לגולפי ולא יהבי להו ניהליה.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65b:2:3.hebrew: דמתני בהדייהו. דאי נמי מצטרו זיקי, לא יהיב להו גולפי.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65b:2:4.hebrew: א"נ פריסדקי נקיטי בהדייהו. כלים רקים לקבל היין היוצא מן הנודות כשהן מתבקעין, דלא איכפת להו אי מצטרו זיקי.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65b:3:1.hebrew: דא"ל למברויא מעיקרא. רב איקא ריש נהרא הוה, וא"ל למברויא לספן מעיקרא הרי ימים רבים: כל עת שיגיעו אנשים הללו, העבירם בחנם.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65b:3:2.hebrew: קיטרי. קישרי. סימן הוא מוסר להם, ומכירם הספן ומעבירם, ואיהו לא טרח מידי.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65b:4:1.hebrew: ידיחם. במים, ואם היו מבוקעות, אסורות.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65b:4:2.hebrew: וכן יין שנפל לתוך החומץ כו' לא גרס.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65b:5:1.hebrew: כל שבהנאתו בנותן טעם. שנהנה בטעמו של איסור, דהיינו בנותן טעם לשבח, אסור. וכל שאין בהנאתו בנותן טעם, שנהנה בטעמו.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65b:5:2.hebrew: כגון חומץ שנפל לתוך גריסין. דנותן טעם לפגם הוא, מותר.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 65b:5:3.hebrew: וכן היו עושין כו' לא גרסי' במתני'.

Shulchan Arukh, Yoreh De'ah 133:3.english: If a gentile hired a laborer and said to him: 'Transport one hundred barrels of liquor for me for one hundred perutot,' and one of them was found to be wine, his entire wage is forbidden, since there is among them the value of one peruta from the wage for libation wine. If it was less than the value of one peruta, it is permitted *ex post facto*. And if he said to him: 'Transport each barrel for one peruta,' and a barrel of wine was found among them, the wage for that barrel of wine is forbidden, and the rest of his wage is permitted. However, *ab initio* it is forbidden to do so.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Avodah Zarah 65.english: In Tosafot and other Rishonim, they discussed the question of why we do not say that our Mishna follows the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who holds that in any such case, everything is permitted except for the value of the libation wine itself, or according to the view of Rabbi Eliezer, who says that one can take from the money an amount equivalent to the value of one barrel and throw it into the sea, and the rest is permitted. Primarily, they explained that they wished to establish the Mishna according to everyone's opinion, and not as the words of individuals (even in a case where some hold that the *halakha* follows them). And also, that the Mishna here is concise in its words and does not differentiate, implying that the entire wage is permitted.

Meaning, the wage for that day's work that was done permissibly. And the Rishonim brought from the Tosefta that *ab initio* it is forbidden to do this work of transporting the barrel with him toward evening. And see in the Rashba, who understood that the intention is that even for free, the matter is forbidden, for anything done toward evening has no wage but rather a benefit, and despite this, the matter is forbidden because the Jew desires its continued existence so that the gentile will owe him this favor (see above 63b regarding one who was hired to break a barrel of libation wine). And in the Yerushalmi, they said that if he did it for a benefit, they seize from the laborer's property an amount equivalent to the wage for that work.

Steinsaltz comment #2 on Avodah Zarah 65.english: Rashi explains that it is after the employer had already become obligated to pay the Jew his entire wage before the transporting of that barrel. And in the Turid, it is written that 'toward evening' is not precise, but rather even in the middle of the day, if the work for which he was hired was completed. And similarly, if the gentile hired him to do completely different work and asked him to transport a barrel of libation wine, it is certainly not the time that is the cause, but rather the fact that the matter is part of the work for which he was hired. And the Rashba wrote (in Torat HaBayit) that 'toward evening' is mentioned here because it refers to someone hired as a laborer for a day's work (and not specifically for this task of transporting barrels), and the novelty is that even though he was hired for the entire day, since there was no time left in the day to do this work — it is not included in the hiring.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 65a:10.english: We learned in the Mishna: If a gentile rents a donkey to carry wine used for a libation on it, its fee is forbidden. But if he rented it to sit upon it, even if the gentile placed his lagin (jug) of wine used for a libation on it, it is permitted. And they ask: Why do I need this additional clause? This is the first clause, as it is the same halakha as the beginning, only with a change in the action! And they answer: The latter clause was necessary to say: He rented it to sit upon it, even if a gentile placed his lagin on it – its fee is permitted, as he did not pay at all for placing the lagin.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 65a:6.english: We learned in the Mishna that if the gentile hired the Jew to do other work with him, and during his work, the gentile told him to transport a barrel of libation wine for him — his wage is permitted. And they comment: And from the general wording of the Mishna, it is to be understood that the law is so even if the gentile did not say to him this thing toward evening, meaning, at the end of the workday.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 65a:7.english: And the Gemara raises a contradiction from what we learned in a *baraita*: If a gentile hires a laborer, and toward evening the gentile said to him: "Transport a barrel of libation wine from place to place" — his wage is permitted. And we infer from there: The reason is specifically when the gentile said to him toward evening — yes, the law is so, that it is permitted, because it is clear that the laborer completed the work for which he receives his wage, and the transporting of this barrel is not related to that. But if he did so during the entire day — no!

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 65a:8.english: Abaye said: When we learned our Mishna as well, we learned it in a case where the employer said this toward evening. Rava said: This is not difficult. This case, where the wage is forbidden if it was not toward evening, is a case where the employer said to the laborer: "Transport one hundred barrels for me for one hundred perutot," for then the transporting of all the barrels is considered one task, and if one of them was libation wine, the entire wage is forbidden due to the wage for libation wine being mixed in. That case, where it is permitted in any event — is a case where the employer said to the laborer: "Transport each barrel for me for one peruta," where the wage for each barrel is paid individually.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 65a:9.english: And so it is taught in a *baraita*: One who hires a laborer, and said to him: "Transport one hundred barrels for me for one hundred perutot," and one barrel of libation wine was found among them — his wage is forbidden due to this mixture. But if he said to him: "Each barrel for one peruta," and a barrel of libation wine was found among them — his wage is permitted.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 65b:1.english: It is related: **He would pour wine** which he sold **to gentiles** from the kankanim (jars) into their wineskins, **and he would go** and **ferry them over the crossing** (i.e., he would transport the gentiles by ferry), **and they would give him the gulfi as his wage.** People **came and told Abaye** to complain that he was profiting from the gentiles' wine. **Abaye said to them: When he labored, he labored with permitted** wine, as he was pouring kosher wine into the wineskins, and only afterwards was the wine rendered forbidden by the gentiles.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 65a:7:1.hebrew: טעמא דא"ל לעיתותי ערב כו' – הא דלא משני מתניתין כרשב"ג דאמר: ימכר כולו חוץ מדמי יין נסך, וכאן נמי שכרו מותר חוץ מדמי חבית. דניחא ליה לאוקמי כרבנן. אי נמי: שכרו מותר משמע כל שכרו. אי נמי בהא, אפילו רבן שמעון בן גמליאל מודי. דהתם אין דרך ליקח יין מן העובד כוכבים, והכא דרך בני אדם ליקח שכר מן העובד כוכבים, ויש לאסור כל השכר. וחילוק זה יש בירושלמי. ולעיל סוף פרק כל הצלמים (עבודה זרה דף מט:) גבי ארג בו את הבגד. ולפי התירוץ דניחא לאוקמא כרבנן, ניחא דלא תיקשי: נוקמה כר"א דאית ליה לעיל יש פדיון לעבודת כוכבים ויוליך הנאה לים המלח אף בלא זה וזה גורם, וקיימא לן כוותיה. ולתירוץ האחר נמי יש לומר: שכרו מותר משמע בלא פדיון.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 65a:9:1.hebrew: הא דאמר ליה העבר לי ק' חביות בק' פרוטות – ובהא אסרה ברייתא כי לא אמר לו לעיתותי ערב, דכל כמה דלא אעברינהו לכולהו לא יהיב ליה מידי, הלכך כוליה אגרא שייך ביה. כן לשון הקונט' משמע. הא אמר ליה לעיתותי ערב מותר, ואע"ג שהיא מאותם חביות שהתנה עמו. וקשה, דמ"מ שכר האיסור מעורב בכל ההיתר. לכן נראה לפרש: ולעיתותי ערב, אחר שהשלים קבלנותו, אמר לו כן. ואשמעינן שאע"פ שלא עשה עמו תנאי חדש, אלא על פי תנאי הראשון הוא מעביר בפרוטה לפי חשבון מאה במאה פרוטות, וסלקא דעתך שהכל שכר אחד הוא ונמצא בשכרו מעורב שכר יין נסך. קא משמע לן דשרי, והוה ליה כמעביר ביום של אחריו מאחר שכבר השלים קבלנותו.
